playbookCommonFailures: Shareholding percentages supplied do not add up to 100% or do not match the share certificates
A shareholder is a trust or company and the natural persons behind it have not been identified
Certified ID copy older than 3 months for one of the beneficial owners
No signed mandate authorising My Accountant to file on the company's behalf
Company has no securities register at all, so there is nothing to upload

informationToProvide.label: Company registration certificate (COR14.3)
informationToProvide.aiHint: Official CIPC CoR14.3, CK1, CK2 or MOI document showing company registration number, registered enterprise name and active directors.

informationToProvide.label: Certified ID / passport copies of all shareholders/owners
alternatives: Certified passport copy for foreign owners
informationToProvide.aiHint: One certified SA ID (Smart Card front and back, or Green Book) or passport per natural person who directly or indirectly holds 5% or more, with a Commissioner of Oaths / SAPS stamp dated within 3 months. Count the owners named in the shareholding answer and flag any owner without an ID.

informationToProvide.label: Personal Income Tax Number for Director(s)
informationToProvide.helpText: SARS income tax reference number of each director / beneficial owner, if known.

informationToProvide.label: Please indicate the percentage of shares held by the shareholder
informationToProvide.helpText: List each shareholder with full name, ID number and percentage held. Percentages must total 100%.
informationToProvide.aiHint: Free-text shareholding table. Must total 100%. Where a shareholder is a company or trust, the client must name the natural persons behind it and their effective percentage.

informationToProvide.label: Share register or share certificates
informationToProvide.aiHint: Share certificates or a securities register showing company name, shareholder names and share allocation. If none exists, the agent drafts one from the shareholding answer (template securities_register).

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Collect ownership structure and beneficial owner identities
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: CoR14.3, certified IDs for every beneficial owner, shareholding percentages totalling 100% and any trust/company shareholder unpacked to natural persons
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: A beneficial owner is a natural person who ultimately owns or controls 5% or more, directly or through other entities. Ask explicitly whether any shareholder is a trust, company or nominee; if yes, request the trust deed / that entity's shareholding and the IDs of the people behind it. Explain in plain language that CIPC now needs this before it will accept the annual return.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Verify identities against shareholding
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: Every owner in the shareholding table has a passing certified ID; percentages reconcile to share certificates or register if supplied
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: Reconcile the shareholding answer against any share certificates: names, ID numbers and numbers of shares must agree. Determine whether the company is an 'affected company' (regulated company under the Takeover Regulations, e.g. listed or state-owned) — for the typical private company it is not, and the filing is the standard BO register. If unsure, flag for Kevin rather than choosing.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Draft beneficial ownership register, securities register and mandate
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: BO register, securities register (if the company had none) and mandate drafted; handoff sheet lists each BO with ID number, nationality, address, % held and nature of interest
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: CIPC requires the securities register and the beneficial interest register as uploads, plus a mandate/POA where a third party files. Populate each BO row: full names, ID/passport number, date of birth, nationality, residential address, email, % of shares, % of voting rights, nature of control (direct shareholding / via trust / via company). Never invent percentages. The mandate is signed by a current director on the CoR14.3.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Send register and mandate to client for signature
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: Signed mandate and signed register uploaded
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: Ask a director to sign the mandate and the register, initial each page, and return as PDF. Tell the client this is what allows My Accountant to file on the company's behalf.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: File beneficial ownership declaration on CIPC
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: BO declaration staged with all owners captured and documents uploaded; Kevin has submitted and the confirmation is saved
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: CIPC e-Services > Beneficial Ownership. Capture each BO exactly as on the handoff sheet, upload the securities register, BO register, mandate and each certified ID (PDF, each under the CIPC upload size limit — merge or compress if needed). Where the company itself is a wholly owned subsidiary, capture the parent and its natural-person owners. ⚠ verify: whether CIPC currently charges a filing fee for BO declarations (understood to be free). Save the confirmation PDF.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Wait for CIPC confirmation
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: Filing shows as processed on CIPC
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: Most BO filings process same day. If a rejection arrives, quote the reason to Kevin and identify which owner or upload it concerns.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Deliver filing confirmation and registers
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: Confirmation, BO register and securities register posted to Communication History
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: Tell the client the BO register must be updated with CIPC whenever ownership changes and re-confirmed with each annual return. Offer the Annual Returns service if it is due.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Final sign-off
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: Kevin confirms the order can be completed
